summary: Regression test after code-quality refactor pass (MD5->SHA-256 in enrichment._stable_score, useCallback/useMemo in auth.jsx/Upload.jsx/IncidentDetail.jsx, module-scope constants in App.js + Login.jsx). All 30 backend pytest cases pass (28 existing + 2 new determinism tests) and all frontend flows pass (all 3 demo logins, pipeline end-to-end, sidebar RBAC for analyst/reviewer/admin). No regressions detected.

minor.issue: Still no file-size cap or rate limiting (pre-existing, flagged in iteration_1).

critical_code_review_comments: enrichment.py::_stable_score: SHA-256 refactor is clean; hex-int mod arithmetic preserves determinism and range. Verified via new TestEnrichmentDeterminism::test_same_input_same_threat_scores (uploaded same log twice, matching IoC values produce identical threat_score).

auth.jsx: useCallback(login/register/logout, []) is safe — closures only touch setUser and localStorage (stable refs). useMemo on context value with correct deps [user, loading, login, register, logout] avoids re-render cascades in consumers. No stale-closure risk.

Upload.jsx: refresh useCallback([]) is stable; uploadFile depends on [refresh] which is stable; uploadSample depends on [uploadFile] which is stable. useEffect dep [refresh] is safe — will not re-trigger interval on re-render. Good pattern.

IncidentDetail.jsx: load = useCallback([id]) is correct — reroute /incidents/:id changes id, load reference changes, useEffect refires. Verified visually: navigating from job-view button to /incidents/:id renders correct incident.
App.js: QUERY_OPTS is declared but never wired to a QueryClientProvider (dormant since iteration_1, pre-existing dead code). Not a regression — flag for cleanup.

Login.jsx setDemo closes over `form` (mode='login', name, role); using functional setState (setForm(prev => ...)) would be marginally cleaner but current code works because setDemo is invoked from a click, not from a memoized callback. Non-blocking.
All refactors preserve identical user-facing behavior and API contract.
